page: Microsoft Azure E128s_v7 is an Esv7-family virtual machine configured with 128 dedicated vCPUs and 1024.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8) for accelerated mathematical and matrix operations. The instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, relying instead on Premium Storage capabilities for external disk attachments.

In benchmark evaluations, the E128s_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance in multi-core processing and high-throughput workloads. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and PassMark CPU metrics all rank in the top 10% tier. Cryptographic and extended instruction execution also place in the top 10%, aided by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instruction sets. Single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics and PassMark memory scores falling into the middle 50% average. Database operations and single-threaded compression tasks show strong performance in the top 25% tier. For memory-intensive key-value operations, the server achieves top-tier results, processing 189.85 million Redis SET operations per second.

The high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dense multi-core architecture make the E128s_v7 highly cost-efficient for large-scale, memory-bound enterprise workloads. It is optimized for large relational databases, in-memory caching layers, and big data analytics where massive RAM capacity prevents disk bottlenecks. Additionally, the presence of Intel AMX instructions enables strong performance in CPU-based machine learning tasks, as evidenced by top-tier prompt processing speeds for large 70B LLM models and strong text generation speeds for medium 7B models. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires careful architectural planning for workloads requiring low-latency local scratch space, and the average single-core performance suggests it is less suited for single-threaded execution paths.
